claims.claim: A versioned source-REPAIR bootstrap intent binds the exact legacy and target generations, source URL, downstream control and pin identity, failed RUN, REPAIR authorization and delivery identity, Executor, and execution-profile selectors.

Admission requires a unique consumed and completed source-bootstrap-v2 lineage bound to the requested FAILURE RUN; active, incomplete, superseded, ambiguous, and mismatched lineage is rejected before target launch.
Source-REPAIR uses a separate exact target activation slot whose TASK-206 production value is closed.
The target checks its bound checkout and exact Git generation before passing the intent’s REPAIR selectors to run_repair_wakeup.
Transport state uses a separate namespace, reads completed migration history without changing it, and does not create a PRIMARY RUN or a transport terminal artifact.
An identical transport intent can replay through the existing REPAIR delivery identity; conflicting or partial transport state is rejected.
The existing source-PRIMARY activation, recovery path, REPAIR wakeup semantics, and roadmap state were left unchanged.
The portability documentation records the post-failed-bootstrap recovery sequence and its mandatory separate target activation.
